title: Echo and Protocol
premise: Gideon Okafor has spent nine years alone tending Earth's derelict seed vault, broadcasting a maintenance beacon no one answers — until a ship in distress transmits in Old Meridian, a language officially extinct since the Reconciliation Wars. The survivors are descendants of the Meridian Exile, the faction history erased, and their message contains proof that the war still burning across the colonies was ignited by a forged transmission Earth's government authored. Hunted by a Protocol fleet that must silence them and shadowed by an exile defector who may be a spy, Gideon must decode the true archive hidden in her own vault's foundation and carry it through the last jump window to the neutral relay at Ceres. She succeeds at devastating cost: the truth ends the war, but exposes Gideon as the daughter of the forger, forcing her to choose between the identity she inherited and the found family she built in the dark.
about_author: Xanthe Eriksen is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete broadcast standards before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted radio station on the Norwegian coast, where she insists the static sometimes sounds like language.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Commissioned
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Establishes her solitary routine in the seed vault: checking seals, logging seeds, maintaining the beacon whose origin records were purged. A quiet chapter of ritual and loneliness, ending when the beacon receives an unscheduled ping. Emotional beat: contentment cracked by curiosity.

chapters.title: A Language With No Living Mouths
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. The ping resolves into a repeating distress call in Old Meridian, which Gideon recognizes only because her mother sang lullabies in it. She verifies it isn't a recording or a test. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past reaching through two centuries of silence.

chapters.title: Nine Survivors
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. A damaged shuttle limps into orbit; Gideon grudgingly grants docking. Nine exhausted exiles emerge, led by Captain Ilsa Vey, who claims they fled a Protocol purge. Gideon's hospitality wars with her instinct for invisibility. Emotional beat: wary first contact, the shock of hearing her mother's language spoken aloud.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ilsa reveals the exiles' purpose: the vault's construction predates official history, and its foundation may hold the original transmission logs from the war's first strike. Gideon denies knowledge; Ilsa doesn't believe her. Emotional beat: suspicion braided with reluctant respect.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Searching sublevel archives Gideon never had clearance to open, she finds her father's name on the vault's founding charter — the man executed as the war's first traitor. Emotional beat: grief reframed; everything she believed about her family inverted.

chapters.title: Protocol Arrives
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. A Protocol cruiser enters the system, ostensibly on routine survey. Ilsa knows it's a hunter; Gideon wants to believe in procedure and law. They argue strategy while hiding the shuttle in a decommissioned silo. Emotional beat: the law revealed as a predator wearing a uniform.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. A lone escape pod lands: Dario Sen, claiming to be a Protocol analyst turned exile sympathizer, carrying partial decryption keys. Ilsa wants him spaced; the youngest survivor, Teo, vouches for him. Gideon casts the deciding vote to trust him. Emotional beat: the risk of mercy.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Teo (youngest exile). Interlude chapter: Teo teaches Gideon Meridian phrases while the others work; found-family bonds form over shared meals of vault rations. Gideon laughs for the first time in years. Emotional beat: warmth as stakes — she now has something to lose.

chapters.title: The Foundation Seal
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Using Dario's keys and her father's charter, they breach the sealed foundation level and find the archive intact — including the authentic first-strike log proving Earth's opening attack was forged. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by horror at what the truth implies.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Sublevel Four
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The Protocol cruiser fires on the surface — someone transmitted coordinates. Evidence points to Dario; he swears his beacon was cloned. Ilsa leads an evacuation deeper while Gideon refuses to abandon him. Emotional beat: trust fractured, loyalty tested under fire.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Starlight
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Hiding in the seed galleries, Gideon confronts Dario privately. He confesses he was sent to verify the archive exists — but defected genuinely when he read the forgery evidence. His handler will burn the vault either way. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a deliberate act, not naivety.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Navigation math: one jump corridor to the neutral Ceres relay opens in six days and won't reopen for a year. The shuttle can't make it repaired and fueled before Protocol reinforcements arrive. They need a diversion. Emotional beat: the clock becomes the antagonist.

chapters.title: Seeds as Decoys
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Gideon proposes sacrificing the vault itself: venting the seed stores as chaff to blind Protocol sensors during launch. The exiles object — it's her life's work. She argues seeds mean nothing if the lie that killed billions stands. Emotional beat: sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: Teo's Run
chapters.summary: POV Teo. Teo pilots the fuel skiff through the debris field to top off the shuttle, nearly dying when a Protocol drone wing sweeps the field. Dario talks the drones down using stolen codes, confirming his loyalty in blood and static. Emotional beat: courage of the young; Dario redeemed.

chapters.title: The Handler's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Dario. Dario's handler contacts him directly, offering full amnesty and revealing he knows Gideon is the forger's daughter — and that Protocol plans to use her bloodline to discredit any archive she carries. Emotional beat: identity as weapon; the enemy knows her better than she knows herself.

chapters.title: Daughter of the Forger
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Gideon tells Ilsa the truth about her parentage, expecting exile from the exiles. Instead Ilsa says Meridian never blamed children for fathers' crimes — but the crew votes on whether she stays. She stays, barely. Emotional beat: rejection faced and survived; family redefined by choice.

chapters.title: Venting Eden
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. The diversion: the vault vents forty years of preserved seeds in a glittering cloud as the shuttle launches. Gideon watches her life's work bloom and die against the stars. Emotional beat: elegy and liberation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Pursuit Through the Corridor
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The jump run under fire; a Protocol interceptor shadows them into the corridor. Dario burns his last stolen codes to spoof their signature, and Teo flies a maneuver no trained pilot would dare. They reach Ceres with minutes to spare, hull scorched. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into awe.

chapters.title: Broadcast at the Neutral Relay
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. At Ceres, Protocol legal attachés demand the archive be sealed pending review — a delay that means destruction. Gideon instead broadcasts the raw logs fleet-wide, unencrypted, in every language including Meridian. Emotional beat: justice seized outside the law, irreversible.

chapters.title: The War That Stopped
chapters.summary: POV multiple, brief rotating sections. Across the colonies, fleets stand down as the forgery spreads; some commanders refuse to believe and fire anyway, but the momentum breaks. On Ceres, Gideon watches casualty feeds flatline sector by sector. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. The tribunal summons Gideon as witness — and as the forger's daughter, expecting recantation. Instead she testifies to her father's innocence and names the living officials who perpetuated the lie. Justice begins, imperfect and slow. Emotional beat: reclaiming inheritance as responsibility, not shame.

chapters.title: Echo
chapters.summary: POV Gideon. Months later: the exiles settle at a rebuilt relay station, Teo apprenticing as a pilot, Dario teaching dead languages to living children. Gideon plants the few seeds she saved and builds a new beacon — this time signed, this time answered. Emotional beat: home as something made, not found.
